assessment.rationale: Free-viewpoint replay has been deployed in some stadiums, but no service lets fans watch any match from any seat or the ball's view, and none reaches 1,000,000,000 fans, so the Main KPI is unmet. Intel True View was installed in about 20 NFL, 8 NBA and 10 soccer stadiums before Intel closed its volumetric studio and sought to sell the unit (https://www.tomshardware.com/news/intel-reportedly-wants-to-sell-its-sports-tech-business). Gaussian-splatting free-viewpoint sports is at research, pilot and early commercial stage, with no verified major-league production deployment (https://journal.smpte.org/conferences/SMPTE%202025%20Media%20Technology%20Summit/20/, https://www.ri.cmu.edu/moving-beyond-the-broadcast/). The NBA's Vision Pro offering is fixed-position immersive video of select Lakers games, replays a day or more later (https://support.watch.nba.com/hc/en-us/articles/20891550821783-Apple-Vision-Pro). Ball-tracking replay exists only in amateur cameras such as BallerCam (https://ballercam.com/blogs/updates/introducing-180-explore-view). Honest limit: multi-camera volumetric replay per venue is known engineering; open problems are camera-sparse reconstruction for any match, live latency and cost, and rights holders control access.
